radar.title: Performance profile
radar.subtitle: Six axes, {{mode}}
radar.emptyBody: Complete at least one test per axis to build the profile.
radar.modeHintPersonalBest: 100 = your best result on this axis so far. Shows form relative to yourself.
radar.modeHintPopulation: Percentile against trained adults of your age and sex.

dashboard.demoNotice: Demo data — no session connected yet.
dashboard.emptyBody: Complete your first test and your performance profile starts building. Relative strength and percentiles also need sex, birth date and body weight in your profile.
dashboard.sportScoresHint: Formed from several tests. The components are measured; the way they are combined is a definition made by this app.
dashboard.noSportHint: BASELINE then suggests exactly the tests measured for your discipline.

badges.demoHint: Sample data. Changes stay on this device.
badges.guestHint: Your data stays on this device only.

welcome.headline: Find out where you really stand.
welcome.body: Sport-specific tests, scientific reference values, a performance profile and the next sensible test — no training log, no calorie counter.
welcome.legal: By continuing you agree to the terms of use and the privacy policy.
welcome.privacy: No account, no email address, no transfer. Your measurements stay on this device and can be exported or deleted at any time.
welcome.accountLater: Accounts and sync are coming later

body.figureLabel: Body view with highlighted performance dimensions
body.detail_population_one: From {{count}} test, compared with trained adults of your age and sex.
body.detail_population_other: From {{count}} tests, compared with trained adults of your age and sex.
body.detail_personalBest_one: From {{count}} test, measured against your personal best.
body.detail_personalBest_other: From {{count}} tests, measured against your personal best.

storage.blocked: Device storage is unavailable (private mode or full). Entries apply to this session only.
storage.migrated: Your data comes from an older version (version {{from}}) and has been carried over. Nothing was lost.
storage.newerVersion: This data was saved by a newer version of BASELINE. It is left untouched until this app is updated — until then it is neither shown nor overwritten.
storage.rejected_one: One record could not be read and is missing from the analysis:
storage.rejected_other: {{count}} records could not be read and are missing from the analysis:

tests.title: Test catalog
tests.intro: Standardised tests with the protocol built in. After each run, 1RM, VO2max, relative strength and pace are computed automatically.
tests.needBodyWeight: Body weight is missing for relative strength.
tests.repsWarning: Above {{limit}} repetitions the 1RM estimate becomes markedly less accurate.
tests.notesHint: Conditions, anomalies, deviations from the protocol.
tests.provisionalHint: This number rests on a definition made by this app, not on a published formula. It will be replaced once documented reference values exist.
tests.chooseSportHint: The tests measured for that discipline then appear here. Without a selection the full catalogue stays.
tests.noSportMatch: No sport found for “{{query}}”. The full catalogue is below.
tests.optionalHint: Useful, but not required for a complete profile.
tests.equipmentFilterHint: Select your equipment — the catalogue then shows what it can measure. With nothing selected, everything is listed.
tests.equipmentNoneDoable: Nothing here can be measured with this equipment. One more item and the catalogue fills up again.

history.title: History
history.emptyBody: Once you record tests, every result and per-test trend appears here.
history.sortNote: “Best” measures the distance to your own best for that test — raw values across different tests are not one scale.

profile.title: Profile
profile.personHint: Sex and age are required for the reference values
profile.sexHint: There are no sound reference tables for "other" — the percentile view stays empty, everything else works.
profile.bodyWeightHint: Kept as a time series: relative strength needs the weight at test time
profile.privacy: Everything lives in this browser only. Nothing is transmitted and no account is created. Clearing browser data also clears these values — that is what the export is for.
profile.importFailed: The file could not be read.

importError.invalid_json: The file is not valid JSON. Please choose the unmodified export file.
importError.unknown_format: This file is not a BASELINE export. Your existing data was left untouched.
importError.newer_version: The file comes from a newer version of BASELINE. Update the app to read it — until then your data stays unchanged.
importError.storage_full: There is not enough device storage. Your existing data is unchanged.
importError.unknown: The import failed. Your existing data is unchanged.

profile.contextHint: All optional. What you put here makes reports and comparisons more precise — guessing would be worse than leaving it blank.
profile.levelWhy: Frames the reference comparison. Without it, the comparison is against trained adults.

levelHint.recreational: Regularly active, without a systematic training plan.
levelHint.trained: Systematic training for at least a year.
levelHint.advanced: Several years of structured training with clear progression.
levelHint.competitive: Competing at regional or national level.

profile.sportPlaceholder: only if none of the above fits
profile.trainingAgeHint: Years of systematic training — not your age.
profile.goalPlaceholder: e.g. build endurance, maintain max strength
profile.constraintsPlaceholder: e.g. left shoulder sensitive under load
profile.constraintsHint: Free text for you or your coach. BASELINE does not assess medical conditions and derives nothing from this — the field exists so the context is known when reading the values.
profile.compositionEmpty: Enter a body weight and the composition appears here.
profile.bmiCaveat: Fat mass and fat-free mass are computed from weight and body-fat percentage, not stored separately. BMI does not distinguish muscle from fat and says little about trained people.
profile.disciplineHint: Determines the suggested test battery. Optional — without a selection the general battery stays.
profile.provisionalHint: These numbers rest on a definition made by this app, not on a published formula. They are listed here so nobody mistakes them for documented ones.
profile.provisionalWeights: Also provisional: the requirement weights of the disciplines. They are derived from each discipline’s load structure — competition duration, rest pattern, dominant mode of work — and not taken from a source.
profile.disciplineTestsHint_one: Plus {{count}} further test to choose from, listed in the test catalogue.
profile.disciplineTestsHint_other: Plus {{count}} further tests to choose from, listed in the test catalogue.
profile.sportsHint: The main sport drives overview and recommendations; further sports get their own tests, references and profiles.
profile.goalHint: Weights the next test suggestion — nothing more.

validation.noBodyWeight: Relative strength cannot be computed without body weight.
validation.repsUnreliable: Above {{limit}} repetitions the 1RM estimate varies considerably.

assessments.title: Assessments
assessments.intro: A test session with a defined scope. Only that makes two points in time genuinely comparable.
assessments.newIntro: Pick a template or compose the tests yourself. On the right you see which axes the session covers — a gap cannot be filled in later without distorting the comparison.
assessments.emptyBody: An assessment bundles several tests into one session and records what scope was measured.
assessments.batteryHint: Compositions for a profile. Ordered by sensitivity to fatigue.
assessments.missingAxes_one: One axis stays unmeasured. The profile will be incomplete.
assessments.missingAxes_other: {{count}} axes stay unmeasured. The profile will be incomplete.
assessments.planHint: Start each test individually. Partial progress is kept.
assessments.finishEarly_one: One planned test is still missing. Completing early is possible; the gap is stated in the report.
assessments.finishEarly_other: {{count}} planned tests are still missing. Completing early is possible; the gaps are stated in the report.
assessments.finishedHint: The session is complete. It can be reopened to add values.
assessments.deleteHint: The session is deleted. The measured results are kept and stay in your history — they only lose their link to the session.
assessments.resultsHint: Percentile against the stored reference, where one exists for sex and age.
assessments.noResults: Nothing has been measured for this session yet.
assessments.summaryGaps: Not measured: {{axes}}. These axes are missing from this session's profile.
assessments.disclaimer: BASELINE is not medical diagnostics. The values describe athletic performance and are neither a diagnosis nor a treatment recommendation. The stored reference values are provisional placeholders and have not yet been reconciled against a published normative sample.
assessments.nextFixed: Set by you. This overrides the app's suggestion everywhere the next session is shown.
assessments.nextSuggested: The app's suggestion based on the usual interval. As soon as you pick a date, your choice applies.
assessments.moreForSportHint: Useful, but not required for a complete profile.
assessments.otherTestsHint: The rest of the catalogue, ordered by capacity.
assessments.generalBatteriesHint: Prepared batteries across all axes — independent of sport. Choosing one here replaces the current test selection.
assessments.noSportHint: Without a sport there is no discipline-specific suggestion. The general assessment below works regardless.
assessments.scopeHint: Every additional test widens the basis: more covered axes mean a more dependable classification and a more complete history. It does not change the precision of the individual measurement.
assessments.alsoIncludedHint: Added from a battery or the rest of the catalogue.

attempts.title: Attempts
attempts.hint: With no entries the single value above is saved. With attempts, the scored value is derived from them — every attempt is kept.

explain.best: The best attempt is scored, with all secondary values from that attempt.
explain.worst: The worst attempt is scored — useful when repeatability is what matters.
explain.mean: The performance value is averaged. Secondary values come from the attempt closest to the mean rather than being invented.
explain.median: The middle attempt is scored. More robust against a single off attempt than the mean.

quality.noBodyWeight: No body weight on file — relative strength cannot be computed
quality.noBenchmarkContext: Sex or age missing — no percentile comparison possible
quality.submaximal: RPE below 8: not taken to maximum
quality.estimatedFromManyReps: 1RM estimated from many repetitions — wider spread

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.intro: What changed over time — and how much that statement can bear. The order is deliberate: a 4 % change across two measurements ten days apart is noise.
analysis.emptyBody: A development needs at least two measurements of the same test. Create an assessment and repeat it after a few weeks.
analysis.confidenceHint: How well is this profile evidenced?
analysis.confidenceFormula: Four parts in equal weight. Deliberately unweighted: a weighting that cannot be justified would be invented precision.

detail.depth: {{deepEnough}} of {{total}} axes measured more than once

analysis.balanceHint: Gap between the strongest and weakest measured axis.
analysis.balanceTooFew: This needs at least two evidenced axes.
analysis.unmeasuredNote: Not counted towards balance because not measured: {{axes}}. Unmeasured is not the same as weak.
analysis.sinceBaselineHint: First against latest measurement per test, with the time span alongside — 4 % in eight weeks and 4 % in two years are not the same statement.
analysis.needTwoPerTest: No test has been measured twice yet.
analysis.changeHint: Direction-adjusted: positive means improved, including for timed tests.
analysis.trendInsufficientHint: A regression line is computed from three measurements onwards. Two points always make a perfect line — that is not a trend.
analysis.compareHint: Completed sessions only. Tests present in just one of the two are marked rather than dropped.

insights.findingsHint: Axes clearly above or below your others.
insights.noFindings: No axis sits clearly above or below the others. This statement needs at least three evidenced axes — with two, one is always the weaker.
insights.findingsMethod: Each axis is compared against the mean of the others, not the overall mean: otherwise a weak axis drags down its own reference. It is named here from a gap of 10 points. Unmeasured axes do not appear — a missing measurement is not a weak performance.
insights.limiterGap: sits {{gap}} points below your other axes
insights.strengthGap: sits {{gap}} points above your other axes

evidence.weak: weakly evidenced — only one measurement so far

insights.nextNone: Once an assessment is completed, a suggestion appears here.

nextBasis.last_assessment: {{days}} days after your last completed assessment. The interval is a default of this app, not a prescription from the literature: it is chosen so a change larger than measurement spread can occur between two sessions.
nextBasis.last_result: {{days}} days after your last measurement — there is no completed assessment yet.
nextBasis.none: No basis for a suggestion yet.

insights.recommendations: What makes the profile more meaningful
insights.recommendationsHint: Ordered by value to the profile's meaningfulness, not by training importance.
insights.noRecommendations: Nothing outstanding — the profile is complete, current and evidenced more than once.

recommendation.add_profile_data: Add sex and date of birth. Without both there is no comparison against a reference, only against yourself.
recommendation.measure_missing_axis: {{dimension}} has not been measured. While this axis is missing, the profile is a fragment.
recommendation.retest_stale: The last measurement is {{days}} days old. It no longer necessarily describes where you stand today.
recommendation.deepen_axis: {{dimension}} rests on a single measurement. A second value shows whether the first was the rule or the outlier.
recommendation.improve_data_quality: {{count}} of {{total}} measurements read only with caveats — usually body weight is missing or the test was not taken to maximum.
recommendation.address_limiter: {{dimension}} sits {{gap}} points below your other axes, based on {{measurements}} measurements. BASELINE measures and contextualises; what you conclude for your training is up to you or your coach.

report.printHint: The report becomes a PDF through your browser's print function: Print → destination “Save as PDF”. BASELINE deliberately ships no PDF library — page breaks, typography and selectable text come from your system this way, and it works offline.
report.gaps: Not measured: {{axes}}. These axes are missing from the profile and must be kept in mind when interpreting it.
report.methodConfidence: Confidence is composed in equal parts of axis coverage, recency, data quality and depth. It is unweighted because a weighting could not be justified.
report.methodNorms: Percentiles rest on provisional reference values of this application (baseline_v0_placeholder). They have not yet been reconciled against a published normative sample and should be read as context, not as a normative finding.
report.methodDerived: Derived values: 1RM by Epley, VO2max by Cooper from running distance. Both are estimation formulas; their spread grows with the number of repetitions and with uneven terrain respectively.
report.brandingHint: Name and logo for printed reports.
report.logoType: PNG, JPEG, SVG or WebP only.
report.logoTooLarge: The logo is too large (at most {{max}} kB). A large image bloats the local store.
report.logoUnreadable: The file could not be read.
report.brandingNote: These details stay on this device and appear only in the report. They change no measurement and no analysis.
report.formulaProvisional: Provisional: defined by this app, not a published formula.

coach.title: Athletes you coach
coach.hint: Manage several people on one device.

roleHint.solo: One record for you alone. No switcher, no one else's data.
roleHint.coach: Several athletes on this device, switchable from the header. Each has their own record, history and reports.

coach.deleteHint_one: “{{name}}” will be permanently deleted along with {{count}} measurement. This cannot be undone. To hide someone without losing data, use the archive.
coach.deleteHint_other: “{{name}}” will be permanently deleted along with {{count}} measurements. This cannot be undone. To hide someone without losing data, use the archive.
coach.privacyNote: BASELINE stores only what you enter about a coached athlete. No account, email address or invitation is needed. Everything stays on this device.

charts.unavailable: The chart could not be loaded. The values are fully available in the table view.

coverage.title: Test coverage
coverage.explain: The reference is the number of tests in the catalogue that feed each axis. An overall value of 82 at 40 % coverage is a different statement from the same value at 100 % — it rests on less.

benchmark.bandCaveat: The band is another rendering of the same percentile, not additional insight. The thresholds (35 / 60 / 80 / 95) are set, not derived from the data.
benchmark.mismatch: The comparison is against trained adults. By your own account you belong to a different group — read the percentile with that in mind.

missing.no_sex: Without sex there is no reference comparison.
missing.no_age: Without a date of birth there is no reference comparison.
missing.no_reference: No reference exists for this test.

benchmark.notValidated: Experimental reference — not reconciled against a published normative sample.

readiness.title: Self-assessment
readiness.sleepHint: As 7:30 or as 7.5 — both are understood.
readiness.sleepInvalid: Please use hours:minutes (7:30) or a decimal (7.5).
readiness.disclaimer: All entries are self-assessments on one day, not measurements. Readiness is the unweighted mean of the questions answered — a weighting could not be justified. BASELINE derives no training clearance and no health assessment from this.

context.title: Conditions
context.hint: Surface, temperature, equipment — optional, but it helps later when placing an unusual value.
context.trainingStatusPlaceholder: e.g. rested, in a build phase, post-competition

testDetail.noResults: No measurement for this test yet.

coachDash.title: Coach area
coachDash.intro: One row per athlete, sorted by who needs attention. The list should set the work, not the alphabet.
coachDash.name: Name
coachDash.method: The trend is a majority decision across the tests for which one can be computed at all — deliberately not a mean of slopes, because percent per 30 days cannot be meaningfully averaged across different tests. “Needs attention” is not a judgement of the person but a pointer to one of the stated reasons.
coachDash.emptyBody: Add the first person under “Athletes you coach” in your profile.
coachDash.soloBody: This area shows several coached athletes side by side. In solo mode it would be a table with exactly one row — the dashboard says that better.

emphasis.title: Emphasis
emphasis.volume: {{minSessions}}–{{maxSessions}} sessions per week, re-test after {{minWeeks}}–{{maxWeeks}} weeks
emphasis.disclaimer: A performance recommendation, not medical or training-plan advice. What is named are the qualities of the axis and a volume as a range — no exercises, sets or repetitions. The time windows are a default of this app, not a prescription from the literature.

flags.outlier: Unusual value — please verify the measurement
flags.efficiency_gain: {{changePercent}} % more output at {{rpeDelta}} points lower perceived effort
flags.threshold: A change counts as marked from 5 % against the previous measurement of the same test. The threshold is set, not derived from the data.
flags.regressionNeutral: A decline is named here just as a improvement is. It can have many causes — daily form, illness, a training block with a different focus.

notes.title: Notes
notes.hint: Free text about this person. Not analysed by the app.
notes.auditNote: The record captures when something happened — not what was there before. A history of all previous states would be a second data store holding the same personal data.

gate.title: Which sport?
gate.body: BASELINE then suggests exactly the tests measured for that discipline — with protocol and reasoning. The entry stays on this device and can be changed at any time.
gate.noMatch: No sport found for “{{query}}”. Choose “General assessment” below — the sport can be added later.
gate.generalHint: Without a sport: one battery across all six axes. Changeable at any time in the test area.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.body: Age, sex and body data decide which reference groups your values are compared with. Everything stays on this device.

sport.title: Your main sport
sport.body: It decides which tests are suggested first and which athlete groups you are compared with. Further sports come in the next step.
sport.noMatch: No sport found for "{{query}}". "General fitness" fits everything not on the list.

additional.title: Further sports
additional.body: Optional. Every further sport gets its own tests, references and profile — the overview stays with the main sport.

goal.title: Your goal
goal.body: Optional. The goal weights the next test suggestion — nothing more. It changes no measurement and no reference.

options.orientation: Just find out where I stand

existing.title: Existing values
existing.body: Optional. If you have results from earlier tests, enter them here — they go straight into your profile with today's date.
existing.none: There are no single-value tests for this selection.
existing.hint: Only tests with a single measured value. Everything else can be recorded later with the full protocol.

result.title: Your {{sport}} diagnostics
result.body: You decide whether to follow the recommendation or look at all tests. The selection adapts as soon as the first results are in.

rating.title: Your rating

gap.no_value: This result has no evaluable value.
gap.no_sex: Without sex no reference group fits.
gap.no_age: Without a birth date no age class fits.
gap.no_reference: There is no robust reference for this test. The value stays comparable with yourself.
gap.anchor_only: The source names only a single anchor, no distribution — that shows a distance, not a level.

rating.caveat: The levels sit at −1, 0, +1 and +2 standard deviations of a normal distribution. They are set, not derived from the data, and a reference value is a basis for comparison, not a physiological limit.

overview.title: Overview
overview.profileHint: 0–100 per axis, from the percentile against the matching reference. The measured value itself stays visible everywhere.
overview.noStrengths: Strengths need at least three measured axes.
overview.potentialBody: The diagnostics so far show the largest room for improvement here.
overview.potentialUnmeasured: No measurement here yet — the biggest gap in the profile.

reasons.never_measured: This test is still missing from the profile.
reasons.overdue: The last measurement is older than the set interval.
reasons.feeds_weak_axis: The test feeds the axis with the largest open information need.
reasons.questionable_last: The last result stands with reservations.
reasons.reference: There is a reference for you — the value can be rated.
reasons.core: Carries the profile of your sport.

overview.emptyBody: Your diagnostic profile is ready. The three tests to start with are below — each takes minutes and gives an immediate rating.

diag.title: What do you want to test?
diag.intro: Choose first, then the list. The database holds {{count}} tests — the ones relevant to you come first.
diag.pickHint: The complete test database with filters.
diag.batteriesHint: Standardised sets. After completion a summarised evaluation is created.
diag.sessionsHint: Bundle several tests into one session.
diag.areaIntro: First the tests of your sport in this area, then all others.
diag.noneInArea: Your sport has no dedicated test in this area.

sport.noStanding: No result for this sport yet.
sport.recommendedHint: Prioritised by what tells you most right now.

battery.startHint: Creates a session with these tests. Each test is started individually; progress is kept.
battery.doneWithin: A result from the last {{days}} days counts as measured.
battery.summary: After completion the app creates a summarised evaluation.

modeHint.manual: You perform the test and enter the result.
modeHint.timer: The app runs countdown, effort time and the end signal.
modeHint.series: The app guides you step by step through attempts or stages.
modeHint.external: The value comes from a device or the lab; the app stores and interprets it.

testInfo.scienceHint: Every row is a named group with a source. A reference value is a basis for comparison, not an absolute physiological limit.
testInfo.noScience: There is no published reference for this test. The app invents none — the value stays comparable with yourself.

result.societyHint: Only when robust data exist. The app forces no artificial comparison.
result.benchmarkHint: Your result against every matching reference group.
result.noBenchmark: No reference group matches this value.

analysisHome.title: Where am I strong — and where is potential?
analysisHome.intro: Strengths, potential, the next sensible test and the performance profile per sport. The deeper evaluation — confidence, balance, session comparison — sits below.
analysisHome.profileNote: These values are not original measurements but a normalised representation (0–100). The measured value stays visible in the history.
analysisHome.benchmarkHint: Your latest result per test against every matching reference group — age class, sex, sport, elite and, where available, the general population.
analysisHome.noMeasured: As soon as a result exists, the comparison appears here.
analysisHome.communityHint: Anonymised comparison with other users — no data yet.

community.title: Anonymised benchmarking
community.body: This is where it will say how many athletes performed a test and which percentile your result sits in — anonymised and only with your explicit consent.
community.statusBody: The app stores everything locally and transmits nothing. A community comparison needs a server that does not exist yet. Until then this says honestly: no data — instead of an invented number.
community.exampleLine: "1,284 athletes performed this test. Your result: 72nd percentile."
community.principle1: No feed, no likes, no flames — a comparison, nothing else.
community.principle2: Benchmark data is handled separately from your data and shared only after consent.
community.principle3: A community percentile replaces no published reference; both stand side by side, with provenance.

historyHome.title: Development
historyHome.intro: Every test over time — absolute and, where meaningful, in percent.
historyHome.calendarHint: When you tested and what is due.
historyHome.emptyBody: As soon as results exist, the development per test appears here.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.intro: Local, no server: the app knows when you last measured. Reminders are off until you switch them on.
reminders.overdueLine: {{test}} has not been tested for {{weeks}} weeks.
reminders.intervalsHint: Interval in days per test. Without a value the default of {{days}} days applies.
reminders.noSuggestion: A suggestion appears from three measurements on.
